newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India down as package falls short.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India down as package falls short.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts came under selling pressure on Thursday as a package of economic reforms announced earlier fell short of market expectations, traders said.
"The announcements were quite pleasing, but the market had expected more," a trader said, adding that trade was relatively quiet.
The GDR market has shown a limited reaction to recent strong local market gains, but it cut its premium to the Indian market after the news.

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram announced the decision to allow foreign portfolio investment in debt and government gilts, among other measures, and said these amounted to a package of economic reforms.
Also, the Securities and Exchange Board of India said late on Thursday it had approved a new takeover code for companies and a stock lending scheme.
A GDR trader said the stock lending scheme could add liquidity to the market.
Traders said the local market was likely to head lower on Friday amid disappointment about the package.
SBI fell 85 cents to $18.75/$19.75, while Reliance shed 50 cents to $14.15/$14.90.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed down 2.38 points at 65.83, with the premium over the local market at 7.86 percent from 10.98 percent on Wednesday.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index closed 15.92 points lower at 3,510.05.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended 0.75 points up at 66.75, a premium of 53.94 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite index rose 12.96 points to 676.52.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended 1.98 points up at 100.48, a premium of 5.64 percent after the Taiwan Weighted Index made 72.44 points to 7,221.98.
